sections.html:
The city of Greenville is the county seat, in the Upstate region of South Carolina beside Interstate 85. It had 70,720 residents in 2020 and an estimated 75,310 for 2025, against 58,409 in 2010. Population dipped for decades and then climbed quickly after 2010.

That recent run-up means many longtime owners have watched their blocks change, and investors call them often. Mill-era worker cottages, bungalows and brick commercial blocks make up a good share of the older housing. Their roofs, wiring and pipes often need attention, and plenty of owners would sooner sell as-is than repair and list.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax inside the city
sections.html:
There is no separate city tax office for this. Greenville County bills every address, and its Tax Collector sits in the South Building, Suite 1100-S (864.467.7050). Pay by January 15 and no penalty applies. For anything about how the city's own levy appears on your bill, ask that office.

DatePenalty step
January 163 percent added
February 27 percent more
March 175 percent more, plus $15.00 execution cost

The schedule is written into S.C. Code 12-45-180. The lien attaches to the property, so any balance left at sale gets settled from your proceeds when the deal closes.

Write to Real Property Services, Greenville County Square, Suite 1000 (864.467.7300). A notice that raises your value by $1,000 or more opens a 90-day objection period counted from the mailing date, per state law.

  • Include the tax map number, your reasons and the figure you think is fair.
  • Mail or hand-deliver it, because email and fax are refused.
  • No notice in hand? The default deadline is January 15.

After the county finishes its review, a 30-day clock starts for requesting a County Board of Assessment Appeals hearing. A loss there gives you 30 more days, counted from the written decision, to take the case to the Administrative Law Judge Division.

sections.h2: What changes when a Greenville house sells?
sections.html:
Selling normally triggers an assessable transfer. The property is valued again as of December 31 in the year of the deed change, the 15 percent increase cap no longer applies, and the buyer's new notice typically comes the following year.

Title on January 1 decides whose name is billed. A deed that changes later puts both names on that year's bill.

Owner-occupants can claim a 4 percent rate and a school-tax credit with an original-signature application filed by January 15. A landlord selling a rental to someone who will live in it therefore hands over a house that can qualify. A buyer planning the reverse, turning a home into a rental, will not get that treatment.

Recording takes place in Suite S-2100 at Greenville County Square, 301 University Ridge. The combined state and county charge under Title 12, Chapter 24 is $1.85 for each $500 of value.

sections.h2: Unpaid tax and the tax sale
sections.html:
Delinquency starts on March 17. An execution notice follows, and the house can be advertised for a public tax sale at the Greenville Convention Center.

A buyer at the sale does not own the house outright yet. For 12 months the former owner can redeem by paying what was owed plus costs and interest that rises over time. Once the year runs out, the bidder gets a tax deed that transfers only the county's interest, with no warranty.

Call 864.467.7050 for this year's sale schedule. A sale before the auction avoids all of this.

sections.h2: Steps to sell a Greenville house with a tax problem
sections.html:
Whether you are behind or inherited a house carrying an old bill, the order below keeps things moving.

  1. Get the exact amount owed from the Tax Collector. It shifts on January 16, February 2 and March 17.
  2. Locate the deed. With an inherited house, collect estate papers too, since title work tends to take longest.
  3. Check that a legal residence application was filed. A missed one can mean the house was billed at the higher rate.
  4. Hand the payoff to the closing agent, who pays the county out of your proceeds on closing day.

Someone paying cash and buying as-is will not demand repairs, so a cottage with tired plumbing or an old roof can still close. A vacant house that sat through a freeze should have its pipes checked before you list.

All of these offices belong to the county, so the same few calls cover any address in the city.

The county accepts payment in person at the Tax Collector's office, by mail or online. Most payments post within three to five business days, which matters near January 15 or any other penalty date. Mail early, or pay in person, if the date is close.

Penalties come off only when the county made the mistake, and you need direct evidence of that. A late bill is not enough, so do not count on a waiver. If you believe the county erred, gather your documents before you call.

The execution cost is a flat $15.00 added at the March 17 step, on top of the 3, 7 and 5 percent penalties. Once that step arrives, the cheapest move is usually to settle the account quickly or sell before the sale is advertised.

Owners of rentals close to downtown workplaces and campuses sometimes grow weary of tenant management. Selling does not demand a vacant or staged unit, but the lease must be addressed in the contract.

Tell buyers whether the house is close to a bus line, an interchange or downtown. I-85 skirts the southeast side, I-185 curves around the south, and I-385 connects downtown with I-26, so commutes vary widely by street.

Thinking of moving out but keeping the house? Ask Real Property Services what renting it does to your bill first. Both the 4 percent rate and the school-tax credit hinge on the home being your legal residence.

sections.h2: Dates and phone numbers to keep handy
sections.html:
• January 1: whoever is owner of record gets billed.
  • January 15: payment deadline, owner-occupant application deadline, and the cutoff for an appeal when no notice was mailed.
  • January 16, February 2 and March 17: penalties step up.
  • March 17: delinquency and an execution notice.
  • 12 months after a tax sale: redemption ends.

Payments and payoffs: Tax Collector, 864.467.7050. Values, appeals and the owner-occupied rate: Real Property Services, 864.467.7300. Deeds: the Register of Deeds at Greenville County Square.

A payoff figure goes stale quickly because the amount grows on every penalty date. Request a fresh one once your closing date is firm.

faqs.q: Which office collects tax on a house within Greenville city limits?
faqs.a: The county Tax Collector. Call 864.467.7050; no penalty applies if you pay by January 15.

faqs.q: What if I sell in the middle of the tax year?
faqs.a: Any unpaid balance stays with the property, and the closing agent takes it from your proceeds. A deed that changes after January 1 puts both owners' names on that year's bill.

faqs.q: What is my window for disputing a Greenville value?
faqs.a: Ninety days from the mailing of a notice that raised value by $1,000 or more. If none was sent, plan on January 15, and put the objection in writing.

faqs.q: Does the city guide differ from the county guide?
faqs.a: Only in focus. The same county offices assess and collect for the city, and the county guide covers all of Greenville County.

faqs.q: Can I still sell a house that was auctioned for taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, while the 12-month redemption window is open. After it closes the bidder can receive a tax deed, so most owners sell ahead of the auction.
